But I was under the impression that you did not have any contacts with the Croat community that had organized itself. Now I'm going to put a question to you. My question will be very concise because time is precious. I will go to the heart of the topic. Does it mean that you did not go see Mr. Mate Boban to introduce yourself to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In addition to being Croatia's ambassador to Bosnia-Herzegovina, I am a private person who's at liberty to engage in conversations with individuals. I said that there had been no official contacts between an ambassador with an organization within Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is not that I avoided them, shrank from them. I was in touch with them in order to see what their pulse was to be able to provide information back to Croatia. Of course, there were individuals who held such views. How much importance should be attributed to that? We are talking about 1991 and the -- there were various scenarios. I said that before, that scenarios changed, that they could have had an impact on the Croatian policy, but there were certain policies that remained unchanged, and I believe that it was Mr. Karnavas who put this question to me in connection with what I stated in my book. I said loud and clear what my dealings in Bosnia-Herzegovina were; among them was the effort to preserve the independence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Therefore, I followed closely what the Croatian state policy was toward Bosnia-Herzegovina. Regardless of what the gentleman from Herceg-Bosna wanted or may have wanted at some point, I provided information to President Tudjman on various matters and events. I don't even know if I was in Croatia at the time of this particular event. What's the date again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: The date is 17th December 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that I'm venturing into some waters that I have not had a personal play in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I misspoke. 27, 27 December 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, you have three or four minutes. Three minutes, let's say, and 31 seconds to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the issue that's been introduced by Judge Prandler is actually one that I had intended to go into myself; however, I think that it's going to take me several minutes to sort of pick up where we'd left off and to get that introduced. And so it may be best at this point just to leave it at that and take up again tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well -- Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we still have one minute, when it came to -- it comes to your count of the time that we spent on the cross, some three to four minutes, I do maintain that what examination I had, it was my cross-examination, and I believe that it should not be deducted from my time. I believe it was cross-examination, all the more so since none of the Defence teams had any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber will deliberate on this matter. I am not able to give you a personal opinion because it's up to the Chamber to decide on this, and you will be informed of our decision. Witness, once again I would like to give you the same instructions as yesterday. Please do not have any contacts with anybody before tomorrow morning, since we shall meet again at 9.00. The Prosecutor used up 49 minutes. We have a lot of time -- he's got a lot of time left, and we will hear you tomorrow. I will leave this courtroom because in a couple of minutes I have another trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of May, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
